message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Run autotest

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 1,13 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [ "main" ]
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'build/**'
      - 'test/**'
      - 'configure.ac'
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Test
        run: |
          sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y git wget
          sudo apt install --no-install-recommends -y curl xz-utils \
            autoconf automake libtool make gcc \
            libseccomp-dev libcap-dev libc6-dev \
            binutils qemu-user uidmap
          git clone https://github.com/RuriOSS/qemu-user-static-x86_64
          chmod 777 qemu-user-static-x86_64/*
          sudo cp qemu-user-static-x86_64/* /usr/bin/

          autoreconf -fi && ./configure
          make test",
  "rationale": "The workflow has a single test job with no explicit timeout, so a hung or runaway run can consume the default 360-minute runner budget. Evidence P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (experiment:batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8) shows adding job timeouts reduced elapsed time by 9.79% on a measured CI workflow fork while preserving all checks. Repository CI history shows successful runs complete in about 6-7 minutes, so a 30-minute timeout provides operational headroom without risking false timeouts on valid runs. The change is minimal, preserves all build/test steps and coverage, and adds no new network access, secrets, or privileged actions.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8"]
}
